purpose: Review published and locally configured limitations relevant to compact snow; select independent geometry and single-crystal comparisons.
redistribution: Original PDFs and publisher HTML remain in ignored research/runs/. This record supplies bibliographic metadata, a limited transcription of numerical fit coefficients in the runner, and analysis; it does not redistribute full papers.

sources.title: Predicting the morphology of ice particles in deep convection using the super-droplet method: development and evaluation of SCALE-SDM 0.2.5-2.2.0, -2.2.1, and -2.2.2
sources.read_extent: Publisher full HTML retrieved; relevant formulation, evaluation and limitations sections read, especially 4.1.11, 7.2 and 9.3.4-9.3.10.
sources.relevance: Authors identify limitations in filling-in aggregation, deposition density, habit, capacitance, collection efficiency and transport coefficients. Section 9.3.8 motivates an offset-contact sensitivity.
sources.limits: Their reported Earth evaluation does not establish accuracy for this prescribed lunar column or our new geometry extension.

sources.title: Structure and falling motion of early snowflakes
sources.read_extent: Original publisher full article text, sections on structure, separation ratio and motion, including the figure captions.
sources.relevance: Small two-crystal aggregates have different contact separation distributions for same-shape and different-shape pairs; a fixed separation of 0.5 is not a universal observed law.
sources.limits: Large flakes were excluded. This dataset cannot directly calibrate large aggregates, mechanical breakup or lunar contact outcomes. Online posting date 2017 is distinct from publication in 1985.

sources.authors: T. Takahashi, T. Endoh, G. Wakahama and N. Fukuta
sources.title: Vapor Diffusional Growth of Free-Falling Snow Crystals between -3 and -23 C
sources.read_extent: Original PDF retrieved; experimental conditions, dimension measurement methods, growth/ventilation discussion and conclusions examined. Table 2 on printed page 24 (PDF page 10) rendered and visually read.
sources.relevance: The -14.4 C single-crystal curve supplies mass and full dimensions over 3-30 min at water saturation and about 1010 hPa. It tests deposition and initialization independently of aggregation.
sources.limits: Planar thickness is inferred from mass and basal area; these are not three independent observations. Empirical fits have no pointwise uncertainties. Laboratory air contains droplets, but this selected 30-minute crystal curve concerns diffusional growth; our control contains no liquid particles or riming.

sources.authors: T. Alena, J. Hallett and C. P. R. Saunders
sources.title: On the facet-skeletal transition of snow crystals: Experiments in high and low gravity
sources.read_extent: Indexed publisher abstract and official NASA bibliographic/abstract record; publisher full-text request returned HTTP 403. A direct request to the canonical NASA citation URL also returned HTTP 403; the indexed official record supplied the bibliographic abstract.
sources.relevance: Airflow and brief reduced-gravity experiments support examining convection and ventilation when transferring crystal habits between gravities.
sources.limits: Abstract-only evidence, with roughly 20-second low-gravity intervals. No lunar snow population, aggregate fracture law or transferable maximum size is established.

code_findings.finding: Native aggregation geometry has no gravity, contact energy or contact-strength argument. Holding one semiaxis while recomputing the other is not a hard maximum-diameter cap.
Native Chen-Lamb density, temperature-selected intrinsic growth ratio and spheroid capacitance determine individual-crystal mass and axes; terminal speed supplies ventilation.
Spherical injected seeds and their fixed number flux are local comparison-adapter assumptions; they are not inferred lunar crystal habits.
Native diffusivity and conductivity remain fixed at reference values rather than following local air pressure and temperature.
The prescribed driver disables atmospheric dynamics and supplies water-saturated gas, a fixed water ceiling and no liquid population. It cannot test turbulence, riming or mechanical ice breakup.

follow_up: Offset-contact full-column sensitivity with exact zero-change parity, conservation, timestep and Earth controls.
Single-crystal Earth laboratory comparison at -14.4 C, then a matched initial-shape and gravity sensitivity; the latter is not a second empirical benchmark.
